narrative:
The model predicts you have an 11% chance of failing your final year, which is low but enough for the school to require you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The three factors that most influenced this decision were your number of past failures, your ambition to pursue higher education, and the size of your family. Surprisingly, having no previous class failures was the strongest element pulling the prediction toward passing. Your clear desire to continue studying beyond high school was the second strongest factor, also pushing the outcome toward success. However, coming from a smaller family (three or fewer members) worked against you. While most students who passed come from larger families (over 65% of passers had more than three members), your smaller household appears to have reduced the support network the model associates with passing.

Taken together, these elements created a slight tilt toward risk in the model’s eyes. To improve your chances, focus on maintaining the strong motivation you already have for higher education. Consider reaching out to teachers or counselors for extra guidance, especially if your smaller family means less daily academic support at home. Building consistent study habits now can help turn that 11% risk into a much safer outcome. (218 words)
